boardProfile.layout: Block Out Level 32 is a symmetrical frame-breaking puzzle. A tall red block formation shaped like a hollow rectangle dominates the center, held in place by cyan `2`-counter blocks on both sides and a yellow `6` cap on top. The solve requires even reduction from both flanks: clear the cyan counters first, peel the outer red columns, and only then drop the yellow cap after the red structure has already loosened.
landmarks: Block Out Level 32 is a symmetrical frame-breaking puzzle.
A tall red block formation shaped like a hollow rectangle dominates the center, held in place by cyan `2`-counter blocks on both sides and a yellow `6` cap on top.
The solve requires even reduction from both flanks: clear the cyan counters first, peel the outer red columns, and only then drop the yellow cap after the red structure has already loosened.

quickTips: Watch the symmetry — if one flank of the red formation looks thicker than the other, equalize before continuing.
The yellow `6` cap is a keystone, not an opener. It drops only after the red columns underneath are thinned.
Think in chain clears. The best move is the one that sets up the next two moves, not just the quickest current match.

steps.title: Move 1
steps.instruction: Clear the left cyan `2`-counter block to open a thin lane on the left flank of the red formation.

steps.title: Move 2
steps.instruction: Mirror that by clearing the right cyan `2`-counter block so both flanks of the red mass are exposed.

steps.title: Move 3
steps.instruction: Start peeling the outer red columns from both edges now that the side lanes exist.

steps.title: Move 4
steps.instruction: Let the yellow `6` cap at the top begin lowering as the red columns underneath thin out.

steps.title: Move 5
steps.instruction: Continue alternating left and right red column work to keep the formation balanced.

steps.title: Move 6
steps.instruction: Once the red mass is mostly separated, feed the freed pieces through the side exits and bottom yellow arrow.

steps.title: Move 7
steps.instruction: Finish with the yellow cap and the last inner red blocks after the frame is broken.

failurePoints: Overworking one side of the red formation while the other stays intact — the red mass shifts into the wall on the undeveloped side and locks the board.
Trying to remove the yellow `6` cap before the red columns underneath have thinned enough, which just reseals the center.
